binders: There exists a real constant c.
Universally quantified thereafter are a finite type ι, a measurable space Ω, a probability measure μ on Ω, and a family X = (X_i) indexed by ι of real-valued functions on Ω.
The universal finite set of indices must be supplied with a nonemptiness witness.
For each such family, the conclusion is universally quantified over every real threshold t.
hypotheses: The constant c is strictly positive.
The finite index type ι is nonempty.
Every X_i is μ-integrable and centered: ∫ X_i dμ = 0.
For every i, the infimum-defined exponential-moment scale K_i = LocalDef001 μ X_i is strictly below infinity in ENNReal.
The family (X_i) is independent under μ.
conclusions: For every t ≥ 0, μ({ω : |Σ_i X_i(ω)| ≥ t}) ≤ 2 exp(−c min(t²/Σ_i (K_i.toReal)², t/max_i K_i.toReal)).
mathematical_definitions: For a real-valued measurable function Y, define K(Y) as the ENNReal infimum of the scales s such that s ≠ 0, s ≠ infinity, exp(|Y|/s.toReal) is μ-integrable, and ∫ exp(|Y|/s.toReal) dμ ≤ 2; measurability of Y is also included in the admissibility predicate.
For each index i, K_i denotes K(X_i) = LocalDef001 μ X_i.
Because ι is finite and nonempty, Finset.sup' gives max_i K_i.toReal.
The event on the left is the set of outcomes for which the absolute value of the finite sum is at least t.
translation.proposition_plain_english: There is a universal positive real constant c such that, for every nonempty finite family of independent, measurable, integrable, mean-zero real random variables on any probability space, provided each variable's infimum-defined exponential-moment scale K_i is finite, the probability that the absolute value of their sum is at least any nonnegative t is at most twice the exponential of −c times the smaller of the quadratic ratio t² divided by the sum of the squared real scales and the linear ratio t divided by the largest real scale.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The theorem applies only to nonempty finite index types; an empty family is excluded by the required nonemptiness witness.
The measure must be a probability measure, and all random variables are real-valued.
Measurability, integrability, exact zero mean, and independence are separate explicit hypotheses.
The scale K_i is defined literally as an ENNReal infimum of admissible parameters; the proposition does not assert that this infimum is itself admissible or attained.
The hypothesis K_i < infinity ensures that K_i.toReal is finite, but it does not explicitly assert K_i > 0. Consequently, a quadratic denominator, the maximum denominator, or both can be zero.

Real division is totalized in Lean, so division by zero evaluates according to the field's total division operation rather than making the proposition undefined. In particular, a zero denominator can make a displayed ratio zero.
At t = 0 the inequality remains part of the statement; with totalized division, both displayed numerators are zero.
The event measure is converted from ENNReal to Real. Since μ is a probability measure, its value is finite.
The same constant c must work uniformly over all finite index types, measurable spaces, probability measures, eligible families, and thresholds.
No identical-distribution, boundedness, symmetry, or common-scale assumption is encoded.
The proposition controls only the absolute tail of the sum and does not encode a one-sided bound or any converse estimate.
